subject: Inference benchmark & unit-cost follow-up (hyperscaler comparison + test plan)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: discovery + initial asks (inference workload)

Hi Anna — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of concrete asks so we can scope the benchmark: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: interactive assistant for field technicians (multi-turn, mix of short prompts and 2–3 long completions per session).
- Expected peak: ~80–120 QPS at peak for short-turns; long-form generation ~10–20 QPS.
- Latency SLO: 95th < 250ms (soft); end-user expectation is sub-300ms for short-turns.
- Data constraints: PII redaction required; prefer VPC/private deployment for the production runway.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm the steady-state tokens/day you want us to budget for? (ballpark is fine — e.g., 50M/day, 200M/day).
2) Are there parts of the prompts that are static across users (we can exploit prefix caching)? If yes, roughly what percent of tokens are static vs dynamic?
3) Which hyperscalers/APIs do you intend to include in the bake-off (AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, GCP Vertex, in-house)?

What we'll do next (proposed):
- Prepare a 48-hour benchmark plan (batch & burst profiles, cache hit rate matrix) and a cost TCO model for: Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved), AWS Bedrock, and OpenAI API.
- Share a short test harness and a sample workload CSV to run the comparisons.

I'll put together the first draft of the benchmark plan and an initial per-1M-token TCO for your review by EOD Friday. If that timeline doesn't work, let me know.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. I attached the sample workload schema we discussed (CSV stub).

Attachment: acme-workload-sample.csv
From: Anna Li <anna.li@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery + initial asks (inference workload)

Thanks Connor — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tokens/day: conservative runway is ~75M/day; if the pilot goes well we test scaling toward 250M/day.
- Static prompt content: roughly 40% of the tokens are stable prefixes (helpful for caching).
- Hyperscalers we will include: AWS Bedrock (Anthropic/Claude and custom models), OpenAI API (gpt-* family), and optionally Vertex AI (we can add if it's low marginal effort).

Key asks before you finalize the plan:
1) Please provide a clear per-1M-token cost estimate for each vendor under a set of assumptions (batch size, cache hit rate).
2) Include model choices/latency expectations (e.g., medium-size LLM vs large) — we care about performance per $ rather than absolute best-quality answer.
3) A simple test harness we can run in our environment that generates comparable traffic across vendors.

We'll loop in our infra lead if we need VPC details. Looking forward to the benchmark plan.

—Anna
Anna Li
Head of Product, Conversational AI
Acme Robotics
anna.li@acme-corp.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme - benchmark & TCO asks (please prep draft numbers + test plan)

Folks — forwarding the Acme thread. They asked for per-1M-token cost comparisons and a runnable harness. Can you help with: 

1) Rough per-1M-token TCO (generation) under three scenarios: 
   - Low batching (avg batch size = 1–2), no prefix cache (0% hit)
   - Moderate batching (avg batch size = 8–16), cache hit = 40%
   - Aggressive batching (avg batch size = 32), cache hit = 90%

   Please provide numbers for: Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved, amortized GPU), AWS Bedrock (typical managed pricing), and OpenAI API. Use conservative GPU utilization assumptions for Dedicated (70% steady).

2) A short 48-hour benchmark plan that covers: steady-state QPS profile (80 QPS short-turns + 10 QPS long-turns), burst to 200 QPS, target 95th latencies to capture, and exact metrics (tokens/sec, avg latency, p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization).

3) Any recommended model/quantization choices to hit sub-250ms p95 for short-turns (e.g., 7B int8 on A100-like, 13B q4 on T4).

Please include: expected wall-clock time to run the tests, expected infra cost for Dedicated runs (per hour), and a small README for the harness (we'll attach this to the email back to Acme).

I'll own the external reply. Flag me if you need anything from product/legal.

Thanks — Connor

Subject: Re: Inference benchmark & unit-cost follow-up (hyperscaler comparison + test plan)

Anna — thanks for the clarifications. Attached are the deliverables we discussed: 1) high-level per-1M-token TCO assumptions & numbers (spreadsheet), 2) 48-hour benchmark plan and harness README (benchmark-plan.md). Below is a concise summary and the proposed next steps.

Executive summary (assumptions):
- Pilot traffic: 75M tokens/day baseline; scale test up to 250M/day.
- Short-turn token footprint: median 25 tokens/request; long-turn median 600 tokens/request.
- Cacheable prefix: 40% of tokens (per your note).
- Target test matrix: batch sizes [1, 8, 16, 32], cache hit rates [0%, 40%, 90%].

Per-1M-token generation cost (ballpark, USD):
- Redwood Hosted (managed):
   - low batching / 0% cache: $9.50 per 1M tokens
   - moderate batching / 40% cache: $4.80 per 1M tokens
   - aggressive batching / 90% cache: $1.10 per 1M tokens
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, amortized):
   - low batching / 0% cache: $3.20 per 1M tokens (70% GPU util assumption)
   - moderate batching / 40% cache: $1.60 per 1M tokens
   - aggressive batching / 90% cache: $0.40 per 1M tokens
- AWS Bedrock (typical managed pricing + network):
   - low batching / 0% cache: $12.50 per 1M tokens
   - moderate batching / 40% cache: $7.30 per 1M tokens
   - aggressive batching / 90% cache: $2.20 per 1M tokens
- OpenAI API (public consumer API):
   - low batching / 0% cache: $5.00 per 1M tokens
   - moderate batching / 40% cache: $3.20 per 1M tokens
   - aggressive batching / 90% cache: $0.90 per 1M tokens

Notes on assumptions: these include model compute, request/response egress, and typical request overhead. Dedicated numbers amortize GPU infra (reserved) + SW license + ops. Hosted managed numbers include our infra margin. OpenAI/AWS numbers are derived from public docs + estimate of throughput configuration. We'll provide the exact cost formulas in the spreadsheet.

Model/latency guidance (to hit sub-250ms p95 for short-turns):
- Recommendation A (low-latency): 7B int8 on NVIDIA A10/A100 class (or equivalent) with batching 8–16 — expected p95 ~120–200ms for short-turns.
- Recommendation B (quality-first): 13B q4 with batching 8 — expected p95 ~220–300ms depending on sequence length.
- If production requires private/VPC, Redwood Dedicated gives the best TCO at scale with identical runtime optimizations.

Benchmark plan highlights (48-hour):
1) Profile runs: 8-hour microbench (single vendor) to verify config.
2) 24-hour comparative run (rolling windows) across vendors with identical traffic generator.
3) 16-hour stress/burst tests (peak to 200 QPS).

Metrics collected: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, throttles/errors, GPU util, batch size distribution, cache-hit ratio.

Attachments: redwood-inference-cost-breakdown.xlsx, benchmark-plan.md, acme-workload-sample.csv

Next steps (agreed):
1) Sign NDA so we can share infra templates & run the harness in your VPC (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/ndas/ACME-8899).
2) Acme infra team to run the provided harness against Bedrock + OpenAI while Redwood runs the Dedicated/Hosted tests (we'll coordinate instance specs).
3) Sync: 30-minute results review the week of Jun 29 (propose Wed 30 Jun).

If this looks good I can send a calendar invite for the sync and loop in our infra engineer to help with VPC setup.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
